approachQuestion.prompt:
Completing a Symbol Square

An n by n grid contains zero for blanks and symbols 1..n for fixed entries. Fill blanks so each row and column contains each symbol exactly once. Return every completion as a grid, once. Fixed entries cannot change. Input fixed entries never repeat within a row or column; nevertheless a completion may be impossible.

Examples:
n=2, grid=[[1,0],[0,1]] -> [[[1,2],[2,1]]].
n=2, grid=[[0,0],[0,0]] -> [[[1,2],[2,1]],[[2,1],[1,2]]].

Constraints: 1 <= n <= 5. No subgrid/box rule applies. Input must not be modified. Return a completed input once if it has no blanks.

options.text: At each step select the blank with the fewest currently legal symbols, using row-major tie breaking. Explore every legal symbol there, setting and undoing row and column flags.
options.feedback: Choosing a constrained cell can expose contradictions early. The heuristic changes search order only; completeness comes from trying every legal symbol and restoring state.

options.text: At the selected cell choose only its smallest legal symbol and never reconsider that value.
options.feedback: On an empty n=2 grid this returns at most one completion although the prompt requires both.

options.text: Enforce different symbols inside each 2 by 2 region as well as rows and columns.
options.feedback: For n=2 every required completion repeats its two symbols in the whole 2 by 2 board; the extra constraint rejects valid answers.

options.text: Enumerate every symbol assignment to every initially blank cell and check row/column uniqueness only after the whole grid is filled.
options.feedback: This is correct but extends prefixes with already repeated symbols. Row/column flags reject those choices immediately.

options.text: Select the first blank in row-major order and explore every symbol absent from its row and column, using the same flag updates and undo.
options.feedback: This is also a complete constraint-pruned search. No variable ordering universally minimizes search on all grids; fixed ordering avoids the minimum-domain scan but can discover conflicts later.

feedback.reason: Choosing a constrained cell can expose contradictions early. The heuristic changes search order only; completeness comes from trying every legal symbol and restoring state.
details: Copy the grid and initialize n by n row/column symbol flags. At each call scan all cells. For every blank test all n symbols against flags; select the blank with fewest legal symbols, breaking ties row-major. If a blank has no legal symbol, reject. If no blank remains, copy the grid. Otherwise recompute the chosen cell’s legal symbols, try each with flag updates and undo.

Choose the blank with fewest legal symbols to expose contradictions early, but still try every legal candidate to enumerate completions. Undo row and column flags with the cell value. An empty domain rejects that branch.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze `acm-b18-22-search` only. Let V count all recursive calls and R count grid entries copied into results. At every call scan the entire n² grid; for each blank test all n symbols, without stopping early on a zero-domain blank. Let B be the sum, over all calls, of the number of blank cells at that call. Full-grid scans cost n² per call, blank-domain tests cost n per blank. Initialize full n by n flag arrays. Do not cache per-cell domains between calls. Choose the tightest stated time and auxiliary-space pair. Count recursion and mutable working state; exclude supplied input and returned output storage, but include copying work in time. Primitive integer/index operations and preallocated-array updates cost constant time; dynamic appends are amortized constant time. No hashing is used unless explicitly stated.

options.text: O(n² + n²·V + n·B + R) time, O(n²) auxiliary space
O(n² + n²·V + R) time, O(n²) auxiliary space
O(n² + n²·V + n·B + R) time, O(n⁴) auxiliary space
O(n³ + R) time, O(n²) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Include whole-grid/domain scans at each call and copied completed grids.
details: Initialization costs n². Every call scans all n² cells and performs n legality checks for each of its blanks; these sum to n²·V+n·B. Recomputing the chosen cell’s candidates is bounded by that call’s blank-domain work. Output copies add R.
Grid and row/column flags use quadratic storage. At most n² assigned blanks/frames are active; each frame retains only selected coordinates and an iteration index, not a separate candidate grid.

Let V count all recursive calls and R count grid entries copied into results. At every call scan the entire n² grid; for each blank test all n symbols, without stopping early on a zero-domain blank. Let B be the sum, over all calls, of the number of blank cells at that call. Full-grid scans cost n² per call, blank-domain tests cost n per blank. Initialize full n by n flag arrays. Do not cache per-cell domains between calls.
“O(n² + n²·V + R) time, O(n²) auxiliary space”: Testing n symbols per blank adds n·B work beyond the cell scans.
“O(n² + n²·V + n·B + R) time, O(n⁴) auxiliary space”: Each frame retains constant state; grids and domains are not copied per frame.
“O(n³ + R) time, O(n²) auxiliary space”: The minimum-domain heuristic does not eliminate branching across many partial grids.
